DELETE /LiveTv/TunerHosts.classification: accepted-divergence, SIDE EFFECT ONLY (the verdict on this row is the configuration read-back, not this): `LiveTvController.DeleteTunerHost` (Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/LiveTvController.cs:1000-1006 @ v10.11.8) rewrites `LiveTvOptions.TunerHosts`, saves, and returns — it queues NO `RefreshGuideScheduledTask`, unlike `ListingsManager.DeleteListingsProvider` (src/Jellyfin.LiveTv/Listings/ListingsManager.cs:83-91) which does. So on Jellyfin the removed tuner's `LiveTvChannel` items LINGER in the library until the next guide refresh prunes them through `GuideManager.CleanDatabase`; on Ferrofin the channel rows are FK children of the tuner host (`crates/ferrofin-db/migrations/0003_live_tv.sql:36-38`, `FK_LiveTvChannels_TunerHosts_TunerHostId … ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the programmes hang off the channels the same way at :60-62, `FK_LiveTvPrograms_Channels_ChannelId`) and go with it in the same statement. Measured on the loop pair 2026-08-30, both servers taking a case-flipped id and answering 204: immediately after the DELETE F reports 0 channels AND 0 programmes (the airings are FK children of the channel rows, so they go too) where it had 2 / 19200, while J still reports 2 / 338. Both servers converge on the SAME end state — Jellyfin's next refresh deletes exactly those rows, because `GuideManager.CleanDatabase` (src/Jellyfin.LiveTv/Guide/GuideManager.cs:147-148, 331-360 @ v10.11.8) removes every `LiveTvChannel`/`LiveTvProgram` the pass did not re-emit, and a channel of a tuner that no longer exists is never re-emitted — and what differs is the window in between, during which Jellyfin serves channels no tuner can stream. Ferrofin keeps the cascade (see the 'don't port Jellyfin bugs' rule): a dangling channel is a 5xx waiting for a client that tries to play it. NOT PORTED, deliberately, and NOT hidden: the journey asserts this op on the configuration, which is what both servers agree the delete means, and this note is the record of what it does not assert.

DELETE /Plugins/{pluginId}.classification: accepted-divergence (NARROWED — the shared ids now behave identically). The previous note said 'a compiled-in extension honestly rejects with 400 where Jellyfin can uninstall any plugin'. The second half was false: `InstallationManager.UninstallPlugin` starts with `if (plugin.Instance?.CanUninstall == false) { LogWarning("Attempt to delete non removable plugin {PluginName}, ignoring request"); return; }` and `PluginsController` answers 204 anyway (v10.11.8). `BasePlugin.CanUninstall` is false for anything whose assembly sits in the server's own directory (BasePlugin.cs:54-55), which is every plugin compiled into Jellyfin's tree — so Jellyfin CANNOT uninstall its five in-tree providers either; it just says 204 and does nothing. Measured on the lane-3 pair before the fix: `DELETE /Plugins/{omdb}` F 400 / J 204. Ported in the F1 review pass and now verified by the journeys.py `j_plugin_uninstall` row (204 + still installed on each server's own read-back, `effect`), together with the version gate (`GetPlugin(id, version)`: 10.11.8.0 -> 204, 9.9.9.9 -> 404, 10.11.8 -> 404 because `Version.Equals` compares four components, notaversion -> 400 from the model binder). A staged WASM plugin IS really removed (file + config + enabled override, restart-required). Admin-only.

GET /Albums/{itemId}/Similar.classification: flat-provider methodology (SET-GATED, order not gateable). Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. WHAT THIS LEDGER ROW DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: `Random` on both sides means the ORDER can never be diffed by any probe, and neither can a page narrower than the candidate pool — parity_diff aligns arrays by Path>Name>Id, so a reordered Items array returns 0 diffs and always will. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GREEN BUT VACUOUS ON THE CURRENT FIXTURE — read this row as 'no divergence detected', not as 'verified'. `suite/perf/gen-fixtures.sh` gave each of the 3 albums a UNIQUE music genre, so the candidate universe is empty by construction on BOTH servers and the leg diffs `{"Items": [], "TotalRecordCount": 0}` against itself. The fixture is changed (two of the three artists now share a genre) but that only takes effect at the campaign's final wipe-and-provision; until that sweep runs, the album matching itself is covered by the `an_album_seed_matches_albums_sharing_a_genre_only` unit test (two albums sharing a genre, a same-genre track that must NOT come back because IncludeItemTypes is [MusicAlbum] alone, and the ExcludeArtistIds leg with a positive control). A real Ferrofin bug found behind this row IS fixed and verified live: album Genres/Studios/PremiereDate are inherited from the album's Audio children (C# AlbumMetadataService + MetadataService.UpdateGenres/UpdateStudios/UpdatePremiereDate); Ferrofin aggregated only album-artist and year, so every album had `Genres: []` and was unreachable by the Genres= query this endpoint issues. After the fix, F album Genres/PremiereDate/ProductionYear match J exactly (Jazz/Rock/Ambient, 2022-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z, 2022).

GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. The scorer half is fixed — the seed's kind now selects the C# provider shape (`MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider` is a flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [MusicArtist] }`, and an EMPTY Genres/Tags pair is not a predicate, so an untagged artist must match every other artist; covered by the `an_untagged_artist_seed_still_matches_every_other_artist` unit test). What still blocks it is the item-UNIVERSE divergence, not the similarity code: Ferrofin materializes MusicArtist as a parentless by-name row with a NULL TopParentId, and every user-scoped `InternalItemsQuery` is scoped to the user's views via `TopParentId IS NOT NULL` (item_repository.rs `scope_to_user_libraries`, the port of C# `AddUserToQuery`), so no artist is reachable by any query that does not name it by id. Detector, both servers: `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=MusicArtist` -> F 0, J 3, while `/Artists?userId=<u>` returns all 3 on both, and adding `&ids=<artistId>` makes the same query return the row on Ferrofin. Same root cause as the MusicArtist/Folder/TvChannel/UserView rows missing from GET /Items/Suggestions. Un-defer path: give the MusicArtist by-name row a TopParentId (Jellyfin's artist rows are physical folder items under the music library, which is why they survive `AddUserToQuery`) — this changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it needs its own change with the perf gate, not a ride-along. ORDERING, for the record: this endpoint's provider orders `Random` on both servers (MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50 / v10.11.8 LibraryController.cs:801) and Ferrofin now emits `Random` too, so when the universe bug is fixed the reads leg must stay pinned at a limit above the candidate pool — the ORDER is not gateable by any probe, since parity_diff aligns arrays by key.

GET /Audio/{itemId}/universal.classification: security-fixed 2026-08-30 (batch S1, cross-user authz): C# RequestHelpers.GetUserId (v10.11.8 Jellyfin.Api/Helpers/RequestHelpers.cs:67-85) has two halves: an absent/all-zero userId falls back to the caller, and a userId that is NOT the caller is honoured only for an ADMINISTRATOR, else SecurityException -> 403. Ferrofin ported only the first half here. Found by the S1 sweep. The handler took no userId at all; it is the audio playback path (v10.11.8 UniversalAudioController.cs:120). Measured: 200 on Ferrofin against 403 on Jellyfin. Re-measured independently in the S1 review pass with a fresh non-admin account ('s1fixprobe', created and deleted on both servers): a non-administrator naming the administrator's id is 403 on BOTH servers, while the administrator naming another user and a non-administrator naming their own id still succeed on both. Recorded in the S1 review pass: the batch claimed these five as flipped but left no row for them, so the fix existed only in the code and the claim. | empty-guid binding fixed 2026-08-30 (batch S1 review pass, reviewer finding F2): ASP.NET binds an EMPTY or whitespace-only value for a `Guid?` to null (SimpleTypeModelBinder), so upstream answers `?userId=` and `?userId=%20` exactly as it answers a request with no userId at all; serde's `Option<Uuid>` tried to parse "" and made both a 400. S1 spread that pre-existing defect to five more routes when it gave previously parameter-less handlers a `Query<T>`. Re-measured on the lane-3 pair BEFORE the fix: `?userId=` and `?userId=%20` were 400 on Ferrofin against 200 on Jellyfin (404/404 where the probe id does not exist). FIXED AS A CLASS, not as an instance: every `Option<Uuid>` field of a `Query<...>` struct in ferrofin-api now binds through `handlers::query_parse::empty_as_none_uuid`. AFTER, the four spellings (absent / all-zero / empty / whitespace) agree on both servers across /Devices, /Channels, /Channels/Items/Latest, /LiveTv/Recordings/Folders, /LiveTv/Recordings/{recordingId}, /Audio/{itemId}/universal AND the four routes that carried the defect before S1 ever ran (/Items, /UserViews, /Persons, /Years). Request BODIES keep serde's strict parse on purpose: System.Text.Json rejects `"UserId": ""` upstream too.

GET /Items/Suggestions.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight legs: seven pinned at a full limit (per type), where Random only permutes and the whole body IS diffed, plus one narrow startIndex/limit leg. That narrow leg is the one place a projection is applied — a page of 3 out of 500 Random-ordered rows draws a different triple per call on BOTH servers (measured: three consecutive calls, three different triples each side), so it compares StartIndex, TotalRecordCount and the page length only. Diffing its Items would pin this row red forever and destroy its ability to signal when the two real divergences below are fixed; the projection is scoped to that leg alone and nothing was added to parity_diff.VOLATILE. Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. The multi-leg probe no longer skips a leg whose servers disagree on status: a status divergence (or a body that is not 200-with-JSON on both sides) is recorded as a mismatch, which is the whole point of keeping the type=MusicArtist and type=TvChannel legs. POST /Plugins/{pluginId}/{version}/Enabl.classification: accepted-divergence: after a successful toggle Jellyfin reports the plugin's `Status` as `Restart` and flips `AutoUpdate` to false, and Ferrofin reports `Active`/`Disabled`. It exists because a .NET assembly cannot be swapped in a running process: upstream's toggle does not take effect until the next boot, and the dashboard has to say so. Ferrofin's toggle takes effect IMMEDIATELY — every consumer reads the enabled flag through `PluginManager::get_plugin` at call time (see `ferrofin-extensions`) — so reporting `Restart` would be a false statement to the client, and per the repo's 'don't port Jellyfin bugs' rule Ferrofin stays truthful. Verified live on the lane-3 pair 2026-08-30: `POST /Plugins/{tmdb}/{v}/Enable` is 204 on both, after which Jellyfin's `GET /Plugins` reports TMDb `Status: "Restart"` and its manifest `autoUpdate: false`, while Ferrofin reports `Active`/`true`. The pre-existing note also stands: a freshly repository-installed WASM plugin 404s until its activating restart while Jellyfin already lists it restart-pending. Admin-only. The version in the path is now honoured on this route too (a wrong version is 404, an unparseable one 400).

POST /QuickConnect/Authorize.classification: security-fixed 2026-08-30 (batch S1, cross-user authz): C# RequestHelpers.GetUserId (v10.11.8 Jellyfin.Api/Helpers/RequestHelpers.cs:67-85) has two halves: an absent/all-zero userId falls back to the caller, and a userId that is NOT the caller is honoured only for an ADMINISTRATOR, else SecurityException -> 403. Ferrofin ported only the first half here. Measured twice on the lane-3 pair (Ferrofin 18396 / Jellyfin 18397) with a second, non-admin account 's1probe' created on both: BEFORE, a non-admin passing ?userId=<admin> reached the manager on Ferrofin (404 for the unknown probe code - i.e. the user gate never ran) against 403 on Jellyfin. This one is a privilege escalation, not only a parity divergence: authorizing a pending request mints a session for the NAMED user on the pairing device, so any authenticated account could hand a device an administrator session. After the fix both servers return 403 for the same request, while an administrator naming another user's id and a non-administrator naming their own id still succeed on both (measured, twice). Regression tests in crates/ferrofin-api/tests/ cover all three cases per route. Fifth instance in this campaign of a C# authorization check Ferrofin served without one (A1 startup, B3 x29 Live TV routes, D2 get_lineups, F1 items); the campaign owes a dedicated audit of every [Authorize(Policy=...)] and RequestHelpers.GetUserId call site in the 10.11.8 controllers against Ferrofin's route guards.

POST /Library/VirtualFolders/Name.classification: accepted-divergence (Ferrofin converges eagerly where upstream defers). The row reads H=True J=False, measured twice on the loop pair 2026-08-30, and the FALSE is the ORACLE'S — but it is upstream's DOCUMENTED behaviour for the request this row actually issues, not a bug, which is why this entry is no longer categorised jellyfin-bug. WHAT THE PROBE ISSUES: `POST /Library/VirtualFolders/Name?name=&newName=` with NO refreshLibrary parameter, i.e. refreshLibrary=false. WHAT UPSTREAM DOES WITH THAT REQUEST: LibraryStructureController.RenameVirtualFolder (v10.11.8 and master byte-identical apart from three added ClearIgnoreRuleCache() calls, plus a [RegularExpression] master added to a DIFFERENT action's name) moves the directory and then, in its finally block, `if (refreshLibrary) { ValidateTopLibraryFolders(ct, true); ... } else { await Task.Delay(1000); _libraryMonitor.Start(); }`. So on refreshLibrary=false Jellyfin deliberately validates nothing and keeps the CollectionFolder row under the OLD name, pointing at a directory that no longer exists, and serves it from /UserViews until some later scan. THE ASSERTION: the journey asserts the ROOT VIEW converges — after the rename no CollectionFolder still carries the old name, the new name is materialized, and the root's CollectionFolder count is unchanged end to end — over /Items + /UserViews. It used to assert only that /Library/VirtualFolders lists the new name, which upstream builds by walking the user-views DIRECTORY (LibraryManager.GetVirtualFolders, LibraryManager.cs:1527-1572, identical in both trees: it matches each directory against GetUserRootFolder().Children by path and leaves ItemId NULL when nothing matches), so it is the one surface a stale DB row cannot corrupt — and both servers passed it while only one was right. WHY FERROFIN MUST NOT COPY IT: Ferrofin derives a CollectionFolder's id from its directory path and get_virtual_folders mints a row for every directory it sees, so leaving the vacated row behind yields TWO rows where upstream has one stale one — measured before the fix as a permanent phantom library ('Movies (synth) Renamed', 5730b9eb5c86a66014cedd6ea527295f) that survived restarts and POST /Library/Refresh and showed up in the client sidebar. FerrofinVirtualFolderManager::rename_virtual_folder now deletes the row the vacated directory backed and runs prune_orphan_collection_folders (the port of ValidateTopLibraryFolders' remove leg — 'If the user has somehow deleted the collection directory, remove the metadata from the database', LibraryManager.cs:1172-1190, identical in both trees — also called from remove_virtual_folder and at LibraryScanner::scan start). CONSEQUENCE, flagged for the owner: the API handler rescans the renamed library UNCONDITIONALLY, not only when refreshLibrary is set, because deleting the old row cascades its children away (FK_BaseItems_BaseItems_ParentId ON DELETE CASCADE) and skipping the refresh would leave the renamed library empty; upstream can skip it only because it keeps the stale row and its children. The rescan is scoped to the renamed library when library_id_by_name resolves its id, which is the normal case (get_virtual_folders mints the row before the lookup); if it does not resolve, the fallback is a FULL library scan — more than upstream queues for this request — and that arm now logs at WARN so an unrequested full pass is attributable. Dashboard-only op. SEPARATE FINDING, NOT WHAT THIS ROW SCORES: with refreshLibrary=TRUE, where the C# above promises ValidateTopLibraryFolders(ct, removeRoot: true), the 10.11.8 oracle still did not converge — renaming 'Music (synth)' to 'Music (synth) DiagRB' left BOTH names in the root for a full 120 s poll at 5 s intervals, i.e. it added the new row and never deleted the vacated one. Only an explicit DELETE /Library/VirtualFolders?refreshLibrary=true pruned it (which is how that measurement was cleaned up, in the same session). That is an upstream bug, recorded here so it is not lost, but it is deliberately NOT this row's category: the probe never sends refreshLibrary=true, and a category must describe the request that was scored. *** HISTORY, so the finding is not lost: batch S1 first measured this as an ORPHAN USER VIEW leak (rename, then rename back, left a phantom library in GET /UserViews that survived a container restart and a POST /Library/Refresh). Batch F3 then found the cause — ValidateTopLibraryFolders' remove leg was never ported, so rows minted from directories on read were never pruned when the directory vanished — and fixed it. The lane-3 branch still carried S1's pre-fix wording at merge time; this row supersedes it.

C# ItemsController.GetItems (ItemsController.cs:307, 525-529) answers a request that is not recursive, names no ids, and whose parent resolves to the UserRootFolder from `folder.GetChildren(user, true)` — not from a query — so no sort, no paging and none of the request's filters apply, and the AggregateFolder's virtual children are APPENDED (UserRootFolder.cs:96-102, `list.AddRange`), not merged into the sort. LibraryManager.GetParentItem(null, userId) resolves an ABSENT parentId to that same folder, so a bare GET /Items is in the branch too. Measured on the lab's 10.11.8 (18097): /Items?userId=…, plus parentId={root} with sortBy=SortName&sortOrder=Descending, with limit=2&startIndex=1, and with includeItemTypes=Movie ALL return the identical seven root rows in the identical order with Playlists LAST, and StartIndex echoes the request. Ferrofin answered the bare form with the WHOLE SERVER (554 rows to Jellyfin's 7), honoured sort/limit/startIndex, and sorted the playlists folder inline (its SortName 'playlists' landing before 'shows (synth)'). Ported 2026-08-30 (InternalItemsQuery.user_root_children, item_repository::user_root_children, and a leading virtual-children-last ORDER BY term in translate_query::append_order_by); all four shapes re-measured live and now agree with Jellyfin on branch, order and StartIndex. THE HARNESS BLIND SPOT WAS REAL AND IS CLOSED: parity_diff aligns arrays of OBJECTS by Path/Name/Id and never compares position, so the misordered row diffed clean; reads.py now runs this op as two legs, both under the existing ADDITIVE with_item_order projection (it adds `_ItemNameOrder`, a list of plain strings, which parity_diff compares POSITIONALLY), and the second leg is the user-root browse itself, carrying the sort/paging/filter parameters upstream ignores.
